subject: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments

Quick update for the week — focused on OKR signals and what we need to lock ahead of QBR. TL;DR: two meaningful wins, one material risk, three asks (two for decisions, one for help).

Wins
- Host infra perf: p95 latency for core text-generation route improved from 210ms -> 165ms after kernel fallback changes; headroom for peak remains ~12%.
- Sales motion: Acme Cloud pilot completed integration test; first 1000 requests matched our SLA in staging (see Acme note below).

Risks / Gaps
- Dedicated capacity: GPU provisioning for Europe cluster is delayed by vendor lead times (ETA slipping 14 days). If not mitigated, Dedicates Q2 SLOs may miss target.
- QBR narrative: we still need one concrete customer ROI datapoint (cost-per-1M-tokens reduction) to make the cost story punchy.

OKR snapshot (owner / % to-date / next milestone)
- Serving runtime (Marcus Lin) — 68% — kernel rollout to remaining fleets by 03/28.
- Dedicated rollout (me) — 54% — EU pool provisioning decision due by 03/22.
- Developer traction (Marissa) — 81% — two new reference apps staged for the QBR demo.

Asks (priority order)
1) Leadership decision: approve incremental EU vendor spend up to $85k to accelerate GPU procurement (decision needed by 03/22).
2) Laura: help secure a short ROI quote from Acme (customer success + procurement intro) — we need an explicit "reduced per-token cost" number for slide 4.
3) Marissa/Vanessa: finalize the live demo runbook and confirm fallback model variant for the demo path (runbook due 03/25).

Attachments: QBR_prep_tracker.xlsx (tracking playbook/tasks), QBR_deck_v2.pdf (current draft).

I will follow up with a short async doc summarizing EU vendor options and the cost tradeoffs this afternoon.

Cheers,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Dedicated Products, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: QBR_prep_tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments

Thanks — good shape.

On the ROI number: I can get Acme to sign off on a brief per-token comparison. Sarah (Acme) is already looped in below; I'll ask procurement for an internal cost breakdown we can quote (will try to have a sound bite by EOD tomorrow).

Decision on EU vendor spend: I'll bring this to the leadership sync tomorrow and recommend approving the $85k tranche if Diego confirms the fastest ETA path.

One ask back: can you add a 2-slide appendix that shows "degradation modes" and our mitigation (fallback, reduced seq length, caching) — that'll help the QBR audience understand risk tolerance.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product
[Attachment: QBR_deck_v2.pdf (pdf, 1.1MB)]

From: Sarah Park <sarah@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments

Laura and Diego — happy to help. We validated the integration and measured throughput and cost internally. Preliminary: we see a 23% reduction in per-request latency with Redwood's new kernel path and estimate ~18% gross reduction in token-serving cost given our traffic profile. Procurement, attaching our internal note.

Let me know if you want a short quote I can sign off for the QBR slide.

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Cloud
[Attachment: acme_exec_note.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments

Diego — adding runbook status:
- Demo runbook draft ready (v0.9) — includes fallback to quantized-gpt-small if p95 > 400ms.
- Playbook includes automated KV-cache warmup script (Marissa) and a manual rollback checklist.
- Need Vanessa to confirm that Console dashboard will expose the demo token breakdown in realtime (Vanessa, can you confirm by Friday?).

Also adding a small win: new sample prompts for the demo improved coherence on long-context scenarios (we'll include examples in the appendix).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Developer Experience

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commander Signalline: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR commitments

Confirmed — dashboard metric for token breakdown will be live in staging by 03/24. I'll add a QuickLook panel for the QBR demo and run a sanity check with Marissa tomorrow morning.

Also — flag: if we approve the $85k path, Console retention for EU pools will increase data retention storage costs; I'll include a table of expected incremental monthly costs in the final procurement note.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Ops Manager
